name: Synchronising lamps
summary: Set of lamps connected between incoming and running phases that brighten and dim with the phase difference during synchronising.
description: Synchronising lamps are connected between corresponding phases of the running system and the incoming machine. As the phase difference changes the lamps brighten and dim, and in the dark-lamp method the breaker is closed when they are dark, showing the voltages are in phase.

Lamps cannot show small residual voltage differences reliably, since a lamp can look dark with a significant voltage across it. They are therefore a backup or visual aid, and the drawing should show a synchroscope or check-synchronising relay for the actual permission to close.
readingNotes: Identify which phases each lamp is connected across.
Look for a check-synchronising relay in the closing circuit.
distinction: Synchronising lamps give a visual indication; a synchroscope shows phase angle and slip direction directly.
